info.name: AssignMate API
info.description:
REST API for **AssignMate** (Assignment Bridge) - students post assignments, verified experts bid and deliver.

### Base URL
Every route lives under `{{baseUrl}}` = `{{serverUrl}}/api/v1`. The health check is the one exception and sits at `{{serverUrl}}/`.

### Roles
`STUDENT` | `EXPERT` | `ADMIN`

### Auth
`POST /auth/login` sets `accessToken` (15 min) and `refreshToken` (7 days) as httpOnly cookies **and** returns both in the response body. Protected routes accept either the cookie or an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header - the collection sends the bearer header from `{{accessToken}}`, which the login test script fills in.

If the access token has expired but the refresh cookie is still valid, the `auth` middleware silently mints a new access token and sets it as a cookie.

### Suggested run order
1. `Health / Health Check`
2. `Auth / Register User` -> `Verify Register OTP` (paste the emailed code into `{{otp}}`)
3. `Auth / Login` - fills `{{accessToken}}` and `{{refreshToken}}`
4. `Expert / Register Expert` -> `Verify Expert` (multipart)
5. Log in as an admin, then `Expert / Get All Experts` -> `Approve / Reject Expert`
6. `Assignment / Create Assignment` -> `Get Open Assignments`

### Multipart routes
`POST /expert/verify` and `POST /expert/student-register` are `multipart/form-data`: the JSON payload goes in a single text field named `body` (stringified JSON), files go under `documents` (max 5). Leave `Content-Type` unset so Postman can add the boundary.

### Variables
| variable | default |
| --- | --- |
| `serverUrl` | `http://localhost:4000` |
| `baseUrl` | `{{serverUrl}}/api/v1` |
| `accessToken` / `refreshToken` | filled by the login test script |
| `otp` | paste the 6-digit code from your inbox |
| `expertId` | filled by `Get All Experts` |
| `studentId` | uuid of a `students` row - needed by `Create Assignment` |
| `assignmentId` | filled by `Create Assignment` |

### Success shape
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "statusCode": 200,
  "message": "...",
  "data": {}
}
```

### Error shape
```json
{
  "success": false,
  "statusCode": 400,
  "name": "Error",
  "message": "...",
  "error": {},
  "stack": "..."
}
```
`name`, `error` and `stack` are only populated when `NODE_ENV=development`.

item.name: Health
item.description: Liveness probe mounted at the server root, outside `/api/v1`.

request.description: Returns `{ "message": "Hello Assignment Bridge V1.0!" }` with status 200 when the server is up.

item.name: Auth
item.description:
Registration, OTP verification, login, password reset and token refresh.

`POST /auth/login` sets `accessToken` (15m) and `refreshToken` (7d) as httpOnly cookies **and** returns them in the response body. The login test script copies both into collection variables so every protected request works right after.

request.description:
Creates a pending user and emails a 6-digit OTP.

| field | rule |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | 3-255 chars |
| `email` | valid email |
| `password` | 6-64 chars |
| `role` | optional - `STUDENT` \| `EXPERT` \| `ADMIN` (defaults to `STUDENT`) |

The account stays unverified until `POST /auth/verify-register` succeeds.

Confirms the 6-digit OTP that was emailed by `POST /auth/register` and activates the account.

Set the `otp` collection variable to the code from your inbox before sending.

Logs in with email + password.

On success the server sets the `accessToken` / `refreshToken` cookies and returns them in `data`. The test script stores both into collection variables, so run this first when you come back to the collection.

Returns the logged-in user's profile.

Allowed roles: `STUDENT`, `EXPERT`, `ADMIN`.

The `auth` middleware reads the `accessToken` cookie first and falls back to the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. If the access token is missing but a valid `refreshToken` cookie is present, a fresh access token is minted and set as a cookie automatically.
Emails a 6-digit password-reset OTP to the address. Always responds `200` so the endpoint cannot be used to probe which emails exist.
Consumes the reset OTP and sets the new password (6-64 chars). The OTP must be exactly 6 characters.

Exchanges a Google **ID token** (not an access token) for an app session. The token is verified against `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`; the email must be verified by Google. A first-time email creates a `GOOGLE` provider user.

> Note: this route has no Zod validation attached, so an invalid shape surfaces as a Google verification error rather than a 400 field error.

Reads the `refreshToken` **cookie** (not the body, not a header) and issues a new access + refresh token pair, re-setting both cookies.

Run `Login` first in the same Postman session so the cookie jar holds the refresh token.

item.name: Expert
item.description:
Expert onboarding and admin approval.

**Multipart routes** (`/verify`, `/student-register`) expect the JSON payload in a single form field named `body` (stringified JSON) plus up to 5 files under `documents`. Do **not** set `Content-Type` manually - Postman adds the multipart boundary itself.

request.description:
Creates an expert account and emails the OTP. Body: `name` (3-255), `email`, `password` (6-64).

Continue with `Verify Expert` to submit credentials and documents.

formdata.value:
{
  "email": "{{expertEmail}}",
  "otp": "{{otp}}",
  "university": "University of Dhaka",
  "department": "Computer Science",
  "ratePerAssignment": 1500,
  "bio": "Final-year CS student, 3 years of tutoring experience."
}
formdata.description: Stringified JSON payload - required by multipartDataValidationZod.
Up to 5 verification documents (student ID, transcript, ...). Pick the files in Postman.

request.description:
Confirms the OTP **and** submits the expert profile plus verification documents in one multipart request.

`body` field (stringified JSON):

| field | rule |
| --- | --- |
| `email` | valid email |
| `otp` | exactly 6 chars |
| `university` | min 2 chars |
| `department` | min 2 chars |
| `ratePerAssignment` | number > 0 (a JSON number, not a string) |
| `bio` | optional, max 1000 chars |

`documents`: up to 5 files, uploaded to Cloudinary. The expert lands in `PENDING` until an admin approves.

formdata.description: Stringified JSON payload - required by multipartDataValidationZod.

request.description:
Lets an already logged-in `STUDENT` apply to become an expert. Same multipart shape as `Verify Expert` but **without** `email`/`otp` - the identity comes from the access token.

Requires role: `STUDENT`.

Admin decision on a pending expert.

| field | rule |
| --- | --- |
| `expertId` | uuid of the `experts` row |
| `status` | `APPROVE` or `REJECT` (case-insensitive - it is upper-cased before validation) |
| `reason` | max 500 chars, **required when rejecting** |

Requires role: `ADMIN`.
Same endpoint as above with `status: "REJECT"`. The `reason` field is mandatory here - omitting it fails validation with `Reason is required when rejecting an expert`.

query.description: See the description table for allowed fields.

request.description:
Paginated, searchable list of experts for the admin dashboard.

| query | notes |
| --- | --- |
| `searchTerm` | free-text match |
| `status` | `PENDING` \| `APPROVE` \| `REJECT` (upper-cased for you) |
| `page` | positive int, default 1 |
| `limit` | positive int, max 100, default 10 |
| `sortBy` | `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `university`, `department`, `ratePerAssignment`, `walletBalance`, `isVerified`, `verificationStatus` |
| `sortOrder` | `asc` \| `desc` |

The test script stores the first result's id into `expertId` so the approve requests are ready to send.

Requires role: `ADMIN`.

item.name: Assignment
item.description:
Assignment creation and the open-assignment board.

> Heads-up: `POST /assignment/create` is currently **unauthenticated** and has no Zod schema wired up, so `studentId` must be passed in the body and must reference an existing `students` row.

body.raw:
{
  "studentId": "{{studentId}}",
  "title": "Discrete Math problem set 4",
  "description": "Need worked solutions for 8 induction and graph-theory problems.",
  "budget": 2500,
  "deadline": "2026-10-15T23:59:00.000Z"
}

request.description:
Creates an assignment in `OPEN` status.

| field | notes |
| --- | --- |
| `studentId` | uuid of the `students` row (FK - a bad id fails at the DB layer) |
| `title` | string |
| `description` | string |
| `budget` | number (Float) |
| `deadline` | ISO-8601 date-time |

The test script saves the new id into `assignmentId`.

> The controller also looks for a Cloudinary attachment under the `attachment` file field, but the route does not mount multer yet - send JSON for now.

Lists assignments with `status = OPEN`, paginated.

| query | notes |
| --- | --- |
| `searchTerm` | case-insensitive match on `title` and `description` |
| `page` | default 1 |
| `limit` | default 10 |
| `sortBy` | any Assignment column - default `createdAt` |
| `sortOrder` | `asc` \| `desc` - default `asc` |

Response: `{ data: [...], meta: { page, limit, total, totalPages } }`.
